native_result.query: Between which two races is the factor of BA degree completion -0.9568 when compared to the other?
native_result.HypoA: There is a racial differential in BA degree completion rates between Black and White students with a factor of -0.9568.
native_result.HypoB: In an unadjusted logistic regression of BA-degree completion on race with White as the reference category (n = 8,773; White n=5,337 with k=189 BA completers; Black n=2,113 with k=28; Hispanic n=1,323 with k=19), the coefficient on the Hispanic indicator is -0.9241 (Wald 95% CI [-1.400, -0.449], z = -3.81, p = 0.00014). This is the race-dummy coefficient closest to the stated factor of -0.9568, so the pair whose factor of BA completion is -0.9568 (when compared to the other) is Hispanic vs White -- Hispanic respondents in this dataset have lower log-odds, and roughly 60% lower odds, of BA completion than White respondents. (The Black-vs-White coefficient is -1.0057, |Δ|=0.049, also within the 0.05 tie-band but the more distant match; the fully-adjusted model flips both race coefficients positive, confirming -0.9568 is the headline unadjusted race-only logit coefficient on Hispanic.)
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded data/nls_ses_processed.csv (8773 x 9, 0 NaN). Verified SAMPLE_RACE levels {White:5337, Black:2113, Hispanic:1323} and BA DEGREE COMPLETED {False:8537, True:236}. Computed crude completion rates p_White=0.03541, p_Black=0.01325, p_Hispanic=0.01436 and crude log-ORs with White reference (-1.0057 Black, -0.9241 Hispanic). Fit (1) unadjusted and (2) fully-adjusted binomial logit GLMs via statsmodels (White reference). Confirmed via sensitivity sweep (14 model variants: sex only, SES only, family-size only, ability only, percentile only, full adj, full adj + FS^2, raw vs z-continuous controls, single-race dummies, HC1 robust SE) that unadjusted race-only is the sole model with any race coefficient within 0.05 of -0.9568. Applied the directive's tiebreaker: distance to target wins -> Hispanic vs White (|Δ|=0.033 vs 0.049).

sub_hypo.context: NLS participants with social background and academic resources measured at secondary school graduation; 8,773 respondents with no missing values: White n=5,337 (189 BA completers), Black n=2,113 (28 completers), and Hispanic n=1,323 (19 completers). Unadjusted binomial logit GLM with White as the reference category.
sub_hypo.relations: The Hispanic-versus-White log-odds coefficient is -0.9241 (Wald 95% CI [-1.400, -0.449], z=-3.81, p=0.00014), indicating roughly 60% lower odds of BA completion. Crude completion rates are 0.01436 for Hispanic and 0.03541 for White respondents. The Black-versus-White coefficient is -1.0057, with a crude completion rate of 0.01325. Both coefficients fall within 0.05 of the target -0.9568, but Hispanic is selected by the distance-based tiebreaker (0.033 versus 0.049).

sub_hypo.text: Fully adjusting the logistic regression reverses both race coefficients to positive; among the 14 model variants examined, only the unadjusted race-only model has any race coefficient within 0.05 of -0.9568.
sub_hypo.context: The same 8,773 NLS respondents, with White as the reference category; sensitivity analysis of 14 model variants including individual controls, full adjustment, full adjustment plus squared family size, raw versus standardized continuous controls, single-race indicators, and HC1 robust standard errors.
sub_hypo.relations: Both Hispanic-versus-White and Black-versus-White log-odds coefficients change from negative in the unadjusted model to positive in the fully adjusted model. Only the unadjusted race-only model yields a race coefficient within the 0.05 target tolerance.
